messages.content: You are a top-tier algorithm for extracting information from text. Only extract information that is relevant to the provided text. If no information is relevant, use the schema and output an empty list where appropriate.

I need to extract information from the following text: ```

My name is Chester. i am 42 years old. My friend Jane is a year older than me.

```

function.name: extractor_extract_information
function.description: Extract information from the provided data array matching a predefined schema, which includes age, name, and optional nickname of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

data.description: An array of dictionaries, each representing an individual's information.

age.description: The age of the person in years. Must be a positive integer.

name.description: The full name of the person.

nick_name.description: Alias or nickname of the person, if available.

message.reasoning:
We have user wants extraction info from given text. We should call the tool with extracted fields: age, name, nick_name? There's mention "my friend Jane" but not necessarily needed unless we want multiple entries. Schema expects array of dicts; each may contain age, name, nick_name.

The text contains two persons: Chester (age 42) and Jane (one year older). So Jane's age would be 43. But do we include both? Yes likely. Provide array with objects containing name and age. Nickname none.

Thus produce JSON like:

[
 {"name":"Chester","age":42},
 {"name":"Jane","age":43}
]

But also note that maybe only one entry? However instructions say "extract information ... relevant". Both names present. Should include both. Also ensure correct format per schema: keys exactly as defined: age?, name?, nick_name?. Use null for missing nick_name? They said default null. Could omit field entirely. We'll provide explicit null.

So output via function call.
